summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with severe COPD, chronic alcohol use disorder, and a history of frequent hospitalizations, was admitted to the MICU with respiratory distress and severe alcohol intoxication. He was hypoxemic on arrival, with a low oxygen saturation of 82% on room air, and required supplemental oxygen and bronchodilator treatments. Imaging revealed bibasilar atelectasis and chronic emphysema, but no pulmonary embolism or acute intracranial process. He experienced significant agitation during withdrawal, requiring sedation with Haldol and lorazepam, as well as temporary physical restraints for safety. Due to his repeated elopements, non-adherence to treatment, and inability to care for himself, a Section 35 petition was pursued. After stabilization of his respiratory status and withdrawal symptoms, he was discharged to police custody for involuntary substance use treatment. His oxygen levels stabilized in the low 90s, appropriate for his COPD, and he completed a course of steroids and antibiotics.
